question: Given $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$, find a $2 \times 2$ matrix $X$ (with real entries) such that $AX + XA = 2I$.
explanation:
Let $X = \begin{pmatrix}x&y\\z&w\end{pmatrix}$, $I = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.

Compute $AX$:

$AX = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}x&y\\z&w\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}x+2z & y+2w \\ 3z & 3w\end{pmatrix}$

Compute $XA$:

$XA = \begin{pmatrix}x&y\\z&w\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}x \times 1 + y \times 0 & x \times 2 + y \times 3 \\ z \times 1 + w \times 0 & z \times 2 + w \times 3\end{pmatrix}$

$= \begin{pmatrix}x & 2x+3y \\ z & 2z+3w\end{pmatrix}$

Sum:

$AX + XA = \begin{pmatrix}x+2z+x & y+2w + 2x+3y \\ 3z+z & 3w+2z+3w\end{pmatrix}$

$= \begin{pmatrix}2x+2z & 2x+4y+2w \\ 4z & 2z+6w\end{pmatrix}$

Set equal to $2I$: $\begin{pmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$

So,

$2x+2z=2 \Rightarrow x+z=1$

$2x+4y+2w=0$

$4z=0 \Rightarrow z=0$

$2z+6w=2$

So $z=0$.

Thus, $x=1$, $4y+2w= -2$ or $2y+w=-1$ and $2z+6w=2\Rightarrow 0+6w=2 \Rightarrow w=1/3$.

So $2y+ 1/3 = -1 \Rightarrow 2y = -4/3 \Rightarrow y= -2/3$

Thus, $X = \begin{pmatrix}1 & -2/3 \\ 0 & 1/3\end{pmatrix}$.

options.A: No, the given condition never implies $AB=BA$
options.B: Yes, the given condition implies $AB=BA$, so $A$ and $B$ commute
